#!/bin/sh
# Stand-in for the GitHub CLI: records the argv it was handed into the project
# (so the two CLIs' calls are compared like any other written file) and answers
# with fixed PR metadata. No network, no credentials, no live pull request.
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> gh-calls.txt
if [ "${STUB_GH:-ok}" = "fail" ]; then
	echo "gh: not authenticated" >&2
	exit 1
fi
case "$2" in
	view) printf '{"title":"a title","author":{"login":"someone-else"},"state":"OPEN"}\n' ;;
	checks) printf 'build\tpass\t1m\n' ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# Deterministic stand-in for git on the `review prepare` path. The cases decide
# what the repository looks like, so nothing here touches a real repository and
# no remote is ever contacted.
case "$1" in
	remote)
		printf 'origin\tgit@github.com:me/fork.git (fetch)\n'
		printf 'origin\tgit@github.com:me/fork.git (push)\n'
		printf 'upstream\thttps://github.com/acme/widget.git (fetch)\n'
		;;
	diff)
		printf 'diff --git a/src/a.ts b/src/a.ts\n'
		printf -- '--- a/src/a.ts\n'
		printf '+++ b/src/a.ts\n'
		printf '@@ -1,0 +1,1 @@\n'
		printf '+export const helper = 1;\n'
		;;
	grep)
		# `path:line:matched source` — the matched text must NOT survive into
		# the impact map, which is what the citation case asserts.
		printf 'src/caller.ts:4:import { helper } from "./a";\n'
		;;
	*)
		echo "stub git: unsupported $1" >&2
		exit 1
		;;
esac
files.gh-calls.txt:
pr view 9 --repo acme/widget --json title,body,labels,author,baseRefName,headRefName,url,state
pr checks 9 --repo acme/widget
